section_summary.extract_value: This abstract reports the development and psychometric evaluation of Brazilian Portuguese translations of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS) and the Intuitive Eating Scale-2 (IES-2) in a cross-sectional sample of Brazilian adults (N = 288). Confirmatory factor analyses (after item elimination and added covariances) indicated adequate model fit, evidence of factorial, convergent and discriminant validity, reliability, and model invariance across sex; men had significantly higher scores on three IES-2 subscales. No mention of 'Study 1' or multiple separate studies is present in the section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Here, we developed Brazilian Portuguese translations of both scales and assessed their psychometric properties in Brazilian adults. A total of 288 participants (men=52.8%) completed the CEMS, IES-2, Body Appreciation Scale (BAS), and a demographic questionnaire. Both instruments' models were found to be invariant across sex, with men having significantly higher scores on three subscales of the IES-2 only.
